The query retrieves programming languages and inventors/creators with images, but it does not actually require a creation year. P571 is optional, so languages without a creation date can still appear. Also, LIMIT 25 prevents listing all matching languages.

It retrieves moons and their P138 namesakes, but it additionally requires a planetary distance (P2244) and performs an unrelated light-year calculation. More importantly, moons without a P138 namesake are excluded, so it does not cleanly answer the requested list of moons and namesakes.

The query does not explicitly require the entities to be settlements. It retrieves entities related to the Way of Saint James and located in the Basque Country, but the results include churches, sanctuaries, etc

Although the question asks for lodges with a Wikipedia article but no label, the query never filters for an absent Wikidata label. OPTIONAL retrieves Wikipedia titles but does not require Masonic_LodgeLabel to be missing.
P31/P279* Q484170 identifies French municipalities/communes, and P948 retrieves their banners.
The result is only one row with a blank ingredient label and count 728. The query fails to produce a usable ranking of individual ingredients, so it does not answer which ingredients are most common.
It counts films per co-actor but does not filter for multiple films (e.g. HAVING(COUNT(?film) > 1)). Also, the returned single row indicates the labels are not properly grouped.
It restricts items to Czechia and retrieves collection-size statements, but it does not establish that the items are art collections.

The query does not exclude a language from being compared with itself—the FILTER (?language1 != ?language2) is commented out. Thus results such as zu → zu are included, which is not an overlap between languages.

It requires the item to be both Q1195942 and a subclass of Q24398318, but the query does not establish that these are specifically Czech buildings. The results visibly include non-Czech locations (e.g. Ballenberg and Hindmarsh).

It identifies items classified as Roman praenomina and counts people associated with them, but it does not actually determine the most common ones: there is no ORDER BY DESC(?ct) or LIMIT, so all 82 are returned without ranking.
It retrieves people buried at Père-Lachaise and their birthplaces/coordinates, but it does not actually organize/group the people by birthplace. It simply orders the results by person label.

It identifies software matching the research/open-source classifications and attaches fields, but it does not ensure the software is specifically research software categorized by field; the classification is too broad and includes items such as GNUnet and Animate.css.

The query never filters for male gender. It groups by gender, but the returned result is a single aggregate row with a blank gender label, so it does not provide average height for male figure skaters in each discipline.

The OPTIONAL block requires all four properties (P1476, P110, P123, P577) to match together. Therefore books lacking any one of them get no title/illustrator/publisher/date information, contrary to "if available."
P27 represents country of citizenship, not necessarily country of origin. Also, the result is aggregated into a single row rather than clearly listing the countries.
The query finds fortifications with Atlas of Mutual Heritage URLs, but it never connects them to either VOC or WIC.
It only retrieves foods that have both an English and a Catalan label, so it excludes many English food types. The Catalan requirement is unrelated to the question.
It retrieves URLs as ?q, rather than the artworks themselves. It also requires a depicted entity with both a label and description, unnecessarily excluding artworks without those properties.
It counts metal bands by country but does not sort or limit by the count, so it doesn't identify the countries with the most metal bands.
The regex restricts words to having each alphabet letter at most once, so it excludes many legitimate long English words. It therefore does not find the longest English words generally.
It retrieves people who received the Theatre World Award, but it does not filter the award date to 2016. The returned years clearly show many other years.

The query retrieves items that are subclasses of Q7725634, but it does not establish that these are all literary works. More importantly, the desc column is actually populated from rdfs:label, so it gives the English label, not the Wikidata description.
